recommendation.plain_language: Keep the shipped adaptive thief. The open question — 'against a strong foreign cop that never places barriers, the shipped thief stays in flee mode; is that right?' — resolves emphatically YES: this run shows even a perfect-information BFS cop cannot beat flee mode (0/120 pooled greedy; 4/60 only under injected cop noise that accidentally drops barriers), while the raw net concedes ~20-27/60 to the very same barrier-less cops. Staying in flee mode against barrier-less cops is not a loophole, it is the optimal branch. Against barrier-placing cops the switch fires (47-49/60 games) and the two lineups are statistically tied; against dedicated best responses both lineups lose regardless. The only cell favoring the raw net is against OUR OWN cop, a co-adaptation artifact that is eps-fragile and does not transfer. Expected match outcomes with the shipped lineup: win vs weak/median/strong-scripted tiers (P 0.87-1.00), lose vs net-quality-thief teams and dedicated exploiters — driven by our cop's evasion gap, not by the thief choice.
recommendation.conditions_that_would_flip_it: SWITCH to the raw net only if we learned most opponents field self-play net cops co-adapted-style with sparse barrier use AND no scripted/BFS chaser fallback (the our_cop-row regime) — every scripted row and both exploiter rows point the other way; even then sticky semantics close most of the gap (14/60 vs 16/120).

caveats: Foreign-cop battery is scripted plus two locally trained best responses; real opposing teams field unknown learned cops — the our_cop and exploiter rows bracket that range, but no un-co-adapted foreign net cop was available to test.

Exploiter rows are LOWER BOUNDS on exploitability: both best responses were plateau-stopped after 7-8 chunks (~1-2 min); a longer or regularized BR could be stronger. Whichever lineup we ship, a BR trained against it reached 117/120 (adaptive) and 120/120 (raw).

p(our cop captures a net-quality thief) = 16/120 uses OUR self-play thief as proxy — co-adapted against this exact cop, so likely PESSIMISTIC for our cop vs a foreign (non-co-adapted) net thief; the strong-net-sensitivity and adversarial tiers may be understated for us.

Match structure assumed an even role split (N=3 sub-games per side of the 6; N=6 also reported); the win condition (win iff our cop out-captures theirs) is N-invariant under Table 1, margin = 20*(A-B).

Binomial win probabilities assume sub-game independence; the sticky adaptive switch violates independence within a match — measured directly instead via the 10x6-match sticky blocks and reported as variants.

The matrix's adaptive column rebuilds the policy per sub-game (switch cleared); real §9 semantics are sticky across sub-games — reported separately (adaptive_sticky_match), and every barrier cop flipped the switch in 10/10 matches, moving adaptive's numbers toward the raw net's, as expected.

Seed blocks 1000-1059 and 2000-2059 are disjoint from the match seeds 7-12; deterministic policy pairs can still lock per-seed on the actual match seeds (the reason for the eps and second-block probes).

The exploiter .pt files live in the session scratchpad (not committed); the earlier exploiter run died before exporting, so both were retrained this session with the builder's recipe (logs: exploiter_log2.txt, exploiter_net_log.txt; finals 59/60 and 60/60 reproduced by the matrix cells).

The adversarial tier assumes the opponent trains a best response against our exact artifacts. This is REALISTIC, not hypothetical: deploy/model/bonus_*.pt are tracked in the PUBLIC repo, so any opponent can clone them and reproduce our exploiter result (~2 min of local training reached 59/60 vs the shipped lineup). Symmetrically, we can do the same against any public opponent repo. Accepted risk for a friendly §9 partner; noted for honesty.

§9 payoff quirk (critic finding): bonus points are win +10, LOSE +7, TIE +5 — a tie is worth less than a loss. Expected-bonus ordering across tiers is unchanged (adaptive 10.00/9.51/6.74 vs raw 9.77/9.40/6.76), but 'P(win)' is not the literal §9 objective.
§9 awards the bonus only if BOTH groups send valid bonus emails AND mutual_agreement=true; an operational failure gives both groups 0 regardless of lineup strength.

The flee-invincibility bound is battery-relative: proven vs greedy-BFS chasers (0/120 pooled), not vs a minimax simultaneous-move pursuer; no learned barrier-less cop was tested. Wilson 95% upper bound for 0/120 is ~3.1% — read P_win=1.00 as >=0.997 under the model, never certainty.
